To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) post-settlement movement is an important phenomenon that can affect estimates of early survival of coral reef fishes, and (2) survival times for mobile species and size classes are longer than for sedentary species and size classes.
(i) juvenile fish can move large distances after settlement; (ii) movement rates are species specific, and (iii) movement can significantly alter survival estimates.

(1) movement of juvenile coral reef fish is common, (2) survival rates of mobile fish are higher than those of nonmobile fish, (3) survival rates calculated from censuses of patch habitats are biased by movement, and (4) survival rates calculated without correcting for movement are lower than rates calculated with movement accounted for.
